title: Practice Exam 1
description: 60 original questions weighted to the Oct 16, 2026 skills measured, including a case study.
scoring: Each question is worth 1 point; multi-part questions are all-or-nothing.

bands.label: Strong
bands.text: You know the material and the traps. Review every miss, re-take in a few days, then book the exam.

bands.label: Close
bands.text: Gaps in specific areas. Re-read the sections listed below and redo the matching labs.

bands.label: Not ready yet
bands.text: Follow the 6-week plan and focus on your lowest domain scores first.

caseStudies.title: Contoso Field Services
caseStudies.html:
Overview

Contoso Field Services dispatches technicians to repair industrial equipment. The company runs Microsoft Dataverse with the tables Work Order, Asset and Technician. Dispatchers use a model-driven app. Customer pricing and invoicing live in an ERP system hosted in Azure that exposes a REST API. Contoso has an Azure subscription with Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions and Microsoft Entra ID, and a Git-based CI/CD pipeline that the engineering team already uses.

Requirements

  1. Work order validation. When a work order is created, a default priority must be set. If the related asset is not covered by a service contract, the work order must not be created and the user must see a clear message. This must hold no matter how the work order is created.
  2. ERP notification. When a work order is closed, the ERP must be notified. The ERP can be offline for hours, no notification may be lost, and the ERP team wants to pull messages when it is ready.
  3. Meter readings. IoT devices send about 2 million meter readings every night. The readings must be stored in Dataverse, removed automatically after 90 days, and do not need relationships to other tables.
  4. Technician app. Technicians need a mobile-friendly React web UI with full control over the design system and routing. It must use Dataverse data, run on Power Platform, and be built and deployed by the existing Git-based CI pipeline.
  5. AI assistant. The data-science team builds a Python agent in Microsoft Foundry that answers dispatcher questions. It must read work orders from Dataverse (read-only) and consult the published Copilot Studio agent maintained by the support team for refund policy.

Technical constraints

  • Integrations must not use personal accounts.
  • Solutions are deployed through managed solutions to Test and Production.
  • The security team prefers generally available features.

questions.stem: A code app must send a user's question to a published Copilot Studio agent and show the reply from the same call. After adding the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector as a data source, which generated method should the developer call?
options: CopilotStudioService.StartConversation
CopilotStudioService.ExecuteCopilot
CopilotStudioService.ExecuteCopilotAsync
CopilotStudioService.ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2
questions.explanation: ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2 returns the agent's response (responses, lastResponse, completed, conversationId). ExecuteCopilot is fire-and-forget (returns only a conversation ID) and ExecuteCopilotAsync can fail with an HTTP 502. The connector ID is shared_microsoftcopilotstudio; the agent name comes from Channels → Web app.

questions.stem: Which TWO plug-in image configurations are valid?
options: A pre-image on the Update message registered at PreOperation.
A post-image on the Update message registered at PostOperation.
A post-image on the Delete message.
A pre-image on the Associate message.
A pre-image on the Create message.
questions.explanation: No pre-image on Create (the row doesn't exist yet) and no post-image on Delete (it's gone). Post-images are available only in PostOperation; pre-images work in all three stages. Images aren't supported for Associate/Disassociate.

questions.stem: A script retrieves 12,000 accounts with the Dataverse Web API. Which approach returns all rows?
options: Send a $batch of three GET requests that each use $skip.
Use the x-ms-dop-hint response header to request more rows per page.
Request the rows with $skip values of 0, 5000 and 10000.
Send Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=5000 and follow @odata.nextLink until it is no longer returned.
questions.explanation: $skip isn't supported by the Dataverse Web API. Control the page size with Prefer: odata.maxpagesize (maximum 5,000) and follow the @odata.nextLink (which carries an opaque $skiptoken) until the last page.

questions.stem: A partner API uses a different base host for each customer region. You must change the host that a connector operation calls at runtime based on a value supplied by the connection, without writing code. Which feature should you use?
options: x-ms-visibility: internal on the host parameter.
The Convert array to object policy template.
The Set host URL policy template.
A custom code script (script.csx).
questions.explanation: Policy templates change connector behavior at runtime without code. Set host URL (dynamichosturl) redirects calls to a host taken from a connection parameter. Custom code would also work but isn't the no-code feature the requirement asks for; Convert array to object reshapes payloads; x-ms-visibility only controls designer visibility.

questions.stem: A code component calls context.device.captureImage when the camera feature exists. It must still load in hosts that don't support the feature. Which manifest declaration should you use?
options: <uses-feature name="Device.captureImage" required="false" />, and check for null before calling the API.
No uses-feature element; call the API inside a try/catch.
<external-service-usage enabled="true"> with the device's domain.
<uses-feature name="Device.captureImage" required="true" />
questions.explanation: With required="false" the component still loads where the feature is unsupported, and context.device.captureImage is simply null so the code can adapt. With required="true" an unsupported host makes the component fail to load. With no uses-feature element the API is null even where the host supports it.

questions.stem: A Copilot Studio agent handles customer emails. It must (1) interpret free-text emails to decide whether the customer is asking for a refund and (2) calculate the refund using fixed policy rules that auditors must be able to reproduce exactly. Which design best meets both requirements?
options: Let the agent's model classify the email and calculate the amount in its generated response.
Use only topics with keyword triggers for the entire process.
Use the model to classify the request, then call a deterministic tool — an agent flow, a custom API backed by a plug-in, or an MCP tool — that calculates the refund.
Put the policy rules in the prompt and ask the model to show its work.
questions.explanation: Use non-deterministic reasoning for interpretation and deterministic components for anything that must be reproducible. Agent flows, plug-ins/custom APIs and MCP tools produce the same output for the same input; a model asked to calculate may vary and isn't auditable. A single agent usually combines both: the model decides which action; deterministic tools perform it.

questions.stem: A flow owned by one employee stops running when she leaves. The team wants flows to use Dataverse without depending on a person. Which approach should you use?
options: Create a Dataverse connection with Connect with service principal (an application user with a least-privilege security role) and make the service principal the flow owner.
Share the flow with the whole company as a co-owner.
Add the application user as a co-owner of the flow.
Store the former employee's credentials in Azure Key Vault and reuse them.
questions.explanation: Create an Entra service principal, a Dataverse application user with a role, and use Connect with service principal on the Dataverse actions. A service principal can be the flow owner but can't be a co-owner. Reusing someone's credentials is neither secure nor supported.

questions.stem: You are migrating a classic ribbon customization to modern commands. Which statement about modern commands is correct?
options: Modern commands require jQuery to reach the form context.
A modern command can build a flyout menu dynamically from JavaScript at run time.
Modern commands are built in the command designer, can use Power Fx formulas or JavaScript functions, and existing JavaScript can be reused.
Modern commands are created with Ribbon Workbench, which is a Microsoft-supported part of Dataverse.
questions.explanation: Modern commanding (GA) uses the in-product command designer with Power Fx or JavaScript, standard solution layering and app/table/global scopes. Dynamic flyouts built from code are a classic ribbon capability, and Ribbon Workbench is a community tool, not a Microsoft product. jQuery isn't supported in form scripts or commands.

questions.stem: An Azure Function app with a system-assigned managed identity calls the Dataverse Web API and receives HTTP 403, although tokens for https://contoso.crm.dynamics.com/.default are issued successfully. What should you do?
options: Create a federated identity credential and run pac managed-identity configure-fic.
Create a Dataverse application user by using the managed identity's application (client) ID and assign it a security role.
Add the user_impersonation delegated permission to the Function app.
Regenerate the function key.
questions.explanation: A valid token with a 403 means Dataverse doesn't recognize the principal or it lacks privileges: create an application user from the managed identity's application (client) ID and give it a security role. Federated credentials and pac managed-identity are for plug-ins calling out; function keys secure inbound calls to the Function.

questions.stem: After a tenant admin created a data policy, a flow that uses the Microsoft Dataverse connector (Business group) and a custom connector to Contoso's inventory API can no longer be saved. The custom connector has not been classified. What should the admin do to fix the flow with the least loosening of governance?
options: Move the Dataverse connector to the Non-Business group.
Delete the data policy.
Move the custom connector to the Blocked group.
Classify the custom connector in the Business group (by name in the environment policy, or by host URL pattern in the tenant policy).
questions.explanation: A resource can't combine Business and Non-Business connectors, and custom connectors default to Non-Business. Classifying the specific connector as Business (environment admins by name, tenant admins by host URL pattern) fixes the flow without affecting other connectors. Moving Dataverse to Non-Business would affect every Dataverse-based resource; blocking the connector breaks the flow further.

questions.stem: For each statement about alternate keys and upsert, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: UpsertResponse.RecordCreated is true when the upsert created a new row.
UpsertMultiple returns an error when two rows in the same payload have the same alternate key.
A Dataverse table can define more than 10 alternate keys.
An alternate key can be used in requests immediately, even while its index status is Pending.

questions.explanation: RecordCreated tells you whether the upsert created or updated. UpsertMultiple errors on duplicate keys in one payload (unlike UpdateMultiple, which keeps only the first). A table is limited to 10 alternate keys, and the unique index is built asynchronously (Pending → In Progress → Active) — use the key only when it is Active.

questions.stem: A custom API runs a long calculation. The caller must get an immediate response and be notified when it completes. Which statement describes the Dataverse approach for background operations (Preview)?
options: Mark the custom API as private so it runs asynchronously.
Register the plug-in asynchronously on MainOperation, which removes the 2-minute limit.
Wrap the request in ExecuteMultipleRequest so it runs in the background.
Call the custom API with Prefer: respond-async to receive 202 Accepted and a background operation ID; completion can go to a callback URI or the OnBackgroundOperationComplete event.
questions.explanation: Background operations run a custom API asynchronously: ExecuteBackgroundOperation in the SDK or the Prefer: respond-async header in the Web API (202 + x-ms-dyn-backgroundoperationid). You monitor or cancel it through the backgroundoperations table. The work is still a plug-in with the 2-minute limit; async dispatch doesn't extend it.

questions.stem: After Application Insights telemetry is added to a code app, no events arrive. The browser console shows: Connecting to 'https://westus-0.in.applicationinsights.azure.com' violates the following Content Security Policy directive. What should an administrator do?
options: Reinstall the @microsoft/applicationinsights-web package.
Add the ingestion endpoint to the connect-src directive in the environment's Content security policy (App tab).
Disable CSP reporting for the environment.
Add the endpoint to frame-ancestors.
questions.explanation: CSP for code apps is configured per environment (Power Platform admin center → Settings → Product → Privacy + Security → Content security policy → App tab) and is enforced by default. The default connect-src is 'none', so outbound calls such as telemetry are blocked until you add the host (a custom value replaces a default of 'none').

questions.stem: When an Account is created, a plug-in must create a related Welcome Task. If the task can't be created, the account creation must also fail and nothing must be saved. How should you register the step?
options: Create, PostOperation, synchronous.
Create, PostOperation, asynchronous.
Create, MainOperation, synchronous.
Create, PreValidation, synchronous.
questions.explanation: A synchronous PostOperation step runs inside the transaction, after the account exists (so its ID is available); throwing an exception rolls back both the task and the account. Async steps can't roll back the operation that queued them, PreValidation runs before the account exists and generally outside the transaction, and MainOperation isn't registerable.

questions.stem: Which TWO changes improve the data-access performance of a code app that lists accounts?
options: Pass select with only the needed columns to AccountsService.getAll.
Use FetchXML to batch the query.
Disable the environment's Content Security Policy.
Retrieve all accounts and filter and sort them in the browser.
Push filter, orderBy and top to the server and page results with maxPageSize/skipToken.
questions.explanation: Microsoft's guidance is to always limit columns with select and to use delegation (filter, sort, top) with paging. Client-side filtering transfers everything, FetchXML isn't supported in code apps, and CSP doesn't affect query performance.

questions.stem: You administer a Power Platform pipeline with Dev, Test and Prod stages. A manager must approve every deployment to Prod before it starts, using a Power Automate approval. What should you configure?
options: Create a personal pipeline in the maker portal and add an approval action to it.
Add the approval to the solution as a business rule.
Enable Pre-export step required on the Prod stage.

Enable Pre-deployment step required on the Prod stage and build a flow on the Dataverse trigger When an action is performed for OnPreDeploymentStarted that reports the result with UpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus.
questions.explanation: Pipeline extensions are gated extension settings that raise Dataverse business events. Pre-deployment step required raises OnPreDeploymentStarted; the flow responds with UpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus (20 = complete, 30 = rejected). Pre-export applies to the first stage only, and personal pipelines created by makers can't be extended.

questions.stem: You register a webhook whose endpoint is an HTTP-triggered Azure Function secured with a function key. In the Plug-in Registration Tool, which authentication type should you choose?
options: HttpHeader
WebhookKey
SAS Key
HttpQueryString
questions.explanation: WebhookKey sends the registered key as a code query-string value — exactly what Azure Functions expects for function-key authorization. HttpHeader and HttpQueryString send arbitrary header or query pairs, and SAS keys are used by Service Bus and Event Hub endpoints, not webhooks.

questions.stem: On the Case form, the Contact lookup must show only contacts that belong to the selected Account, and the filter must be applied every time the user opens the lookup. Which registration approach should you use?
options: A static OnLoad handler that calls Xrm.WebApi.retrieveMultipleRecords and rebuilds the lookup.
Dynamically register a handler with addPreSearch on the Contact lookup control and call addCustomFilter inside the handler.
Edit the form XML to add the filter, and republish after each change.
A static OnChange handler on the Account column that sets the Contact column to null.
questions.explanation: Lookup filtering is done in the PreSearch event, which has no form-designer registration surface, so you register it dynamically with addPreSearch and apply the FetchXML filter with addCustomFilter in the callback. Static handlers are for logic that must always run on specific form events (OnLoad, OnSave, OnChange).

questions.stem: For each statement about the Dataverse event execution pipeline, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: An ISV can register a step on the MainOperation stage (30) of a standard table message such as Create.
Asynchronous execution mode can be selected only for steps registered on PostOperation.
Synchronous PostOperation steps run inside the database transaction of the operation.
PreValidation steps run after the user's security privilege checks.

questions.explanation: Registerable stages are PreValidation (10), PreOperation (20) and PostOperation (40); MainOperation (30) is internal (the exception is the plug-in type linked to a custom API). Async is valid only on PostOperation. Sync PreOperation and PostOperation run inside the transaction. PreValidation runs before the privilege checks.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps to let a Dataverse plug-in call Azure Key Vault by using Power Platform managed identity.
items: Create the user-assigned managed identity (or app registration) in Microsoft Entra ID.
Build, sign and register the plug-in package or assembly.
Add a federated identity credential for the plug-in on the identity in Microsoft Entra ID.
Create the managedidentity record in Dataverse and link it to the plug-in.
Grant the identity access to the Key Vault.
questions.explanation: The documented setup is: create the identity, build/sign/register the plug-in (signing is mandatory because the certificate feeds the credential subject), add the federated identity credential, create and link the Dataverse managedidentity record, then grant Azure access and test. At run time the plug-in calls IManagedIdentityService.AcquireToken(scopes).

questions.stem: Operations needs an alert within minutes when production cloud flows fail. The environment is a Managed Environment. The built-in Power Platform admin center Monitor alerts only evaluate once every 24 hours. What should you recommend?
options: Add a Terminate action to every flow.
Set PluginTraceLogSetting to All for the environment.
Keep the built-in alerts and lower the threshold.
Export telemetry to Application Insights and create an Azure Monitor alert rule with an action group on the failures.
questions.explanation: Built-in Monitor alerts use 24-hour aggregates evaluated once per 24 hours (and only on managed environments). For near-real-time alerting, export telemetry to Application Insights and use Azure Monitor alert rules and action groups. The plug-in trace log only records plug-in activity, and Terminate doesn't notify anyone.

questions.stem: You call Xrm.WebApi.online.executeMultiple from a model-driven app script. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: One call can contain up to 1,000 requests.
Wrapping requests in an inner array makes them a single transactional change set.
A retrieve (read) request can be included inside a change set.

questions.explanation: executeMultiple accepts up to 1,000 requests per batch. An array inside the outer array forms a transactional change set, but OData v4 doesn't allow read operations inside a change set. Don't confuse the 1,000-request batch cap with the 5,000-row page size of retrieveMultipleRecords (500 for elastic tables).

questions.stem: Validation logic is registered as a synchronous plug-in step on the Create message of the Account table. A new integration will insert accounts by calling CreateMultiple. What should you expect?
options: The Create step doesn't run; you must register the logic again on CreateMultiple.
The Create step still runs once for each account in the batch.
The CreateMultiple call fails because a Create step exists.
The Create step runs once for the whole batch with an EntityCollection target.
questions.explanation: Dataverse merges the pipelines: a step registered on Create still fires once per record when CreateMultiple is used. Register a step on CreateMultiple only to gain batch-level processing performance, and then avoid running the same logic twice.

questions.stem: A listener must return a processed result string to Dataverse as part of the operation. Which TWO service endpoint contracts support returning data?
options: Topic
Event Hub
REST
Queue
Two-way
questions.explanation: Only the Two-way and REST contracts return data to Dataverse. Queue and Topic buffer messages, One-way posts without a response, and Event Hub is a one-direction streaming ingestion endpoint.

questions.stem: A Foundry agent must use Microsoft 365 work context (mail, meetings, files) for the signed-in user. Which statement about Work IQ is correct?
options: Work IQ replaces the Dataverse MCP server for reading Dataverse tables.
Work IQ is available only inside Copilot Studio.
The Work IQ tool inside Foundry Agent Service is Preview, the Work IQ MCP endpoint is GA, and calls use on-behalf-of access for the signed-in user.
Work IQ uses application-only permissions and returns tenant-wide data regardless of the user.
questions.explanation: Work IQ's status is surface-dependent: the Work IQ MCP endpoint is GA, while the Work IQ tool in Foundry (work_iq_preview), Work IQ in Copilot Studio and Business Applications in Work IQ are Preview. Foundry forwards the call over A2A with on-behalf-of of the signed-in user, so Microsoft 365 permissions and sensitivity labels are honored.

questions.stem: A code app reads a SharePoint list whose site and list differ between Dev, Test and Prod. The solution is deployed with pipelines. How should you add the data source so the app is portable without code changes?
options: Edit power.config.json by hand in each environment.
Hard-code the site URL and switch it with PA_CLI_ENVIRONMENT_ID in the CI pipeline.
Reference solution environment variables in the data source arguments, for example --dataset "@envvar:contoso_SiteUrl" --table "@envvar:contoso_ListName".
Create a separate code app for each environment.
questions.explanation: Solution environment variables are referenced from data-source arguments with the @envvar:<schemaname> prefix, so each environment's current value is used. PA_CLI_* variables configure the CLI/CI run (environment ID, solution ID, service principal) — they are a different concept and don't parameterize a data source.

questions.stem: Which TWO changes improve the performance and reliability of a plug-in?
options: Cache the previously retrieved record in a static field to avoid repeated queries.
Start several threads to run independent queries in parallel.
Wrap bulk updates in ExecuteMultipleRequest inside the plug-in.
Limit the columns in retrieves and images to those the logic needs.
Set filtering attributes on the Update step so it runs only when relevant columns change.
questions.explanation: Filtering attributes prevent unnecessary executions and restricted columns reduce data volume. Plug-ins must be stateless (instances are cached and reused across threads), batch request types shouldn't be used inside plug-ins, and parallel/multi-threaded code is unsupported in the sandbox.

questions.stem: Contoso must guarantee that no Opportunity is saved with a discount above 20% unless an approval flag is set — whether the record is created from the app, an Excel import, a cloud flow or the Web API. The rule must read the credit status stored on a different table. Which implementation should you choose?
options: A synchronous plug-in registered on the Opportunity Create and Update messages.
A business rule that shows an error message on the form.
A JavaScript OnSave handler on the Opportunity form.
A cloud flow that runs when a row is modified and reverts the discount.
questions.explanation: A synchronous plug-in is server-trusted, runs for every entry point (app, import, flow, API) and can block the save by throwing InvalidPluginExecutionException. Client script and form business rules only run in the UI and can be bypassed. A flow runs after the save, so it can't prevent invalid data from being committed.

questions.stem: A code app initialized with pa app init must read and write Dataverse accounts and contacts and call the Office 365 Users connector. Which approach is correct?
options: Add the tables to power.config.json by hand and run npm run build.
Run pac code add-data-source for each table and connector.
Run pa app add data-source --connector dataverse --table account --table contact once, then add the Office 365 Users connector.

Run pa app add data-source --connector dataverse --table account and again with --table contact; create a connection for Office 365 Users and run pa app add data-source --connector shared_office365users.
questions.explanation: Native Dataverse supports one table per add data-source command (repeat --table works only for connector tables that share a connection and dataset). Connector data sources need a connection first (pa connection create). pac code ... is the legacy/Preview CLI. The command generates AccountsService/AccountsModel files under src/generated.

questions.stem: Complete the plug-in code that posts the execution context to a registered Azure Service Bus endpoint.
questions.template:
var notify = (IServiceEndpointNotificationService)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof({1}));
string reply = notify.{2}(new EntityReference("serviceendpoint", endpointId), context);

options: IOrganizationService
IServiceEndpointFactory
IServiceEndpointNotificationService
ITracingService
Execute
Send
Publish
Notify

questions.explanation: IServiceEndpointNotificationService has a single method, Execute(EntityReference serviceEndpoint, IExecutionContext context), which posts the current execution context (a serialized RemoteExecutionContext) to the registered ServiceEndpoint and returns the endpoint's response string.

questions.stem: A custom API with no plug-in was added to the catalog as a Dataverse business event. Which Power Automate trigger starts a flow when the event is raised?
options: When a business event occurs
When an HTTP request is received
When an action is performed
When a row is added, modified or deleted
questions.explanation: The Dataverse connector trigger for business events and custom APIs is When an action is performed (parameters: Catalog, Category, Table name, Action name). When a row is added, modified or deleted handles ordinary row events; “When a business event occurs” belongs to Finance & Operations.

questions.stem: A dataset PCF component reads context.parameters.items.records inside init and always gets an empty collection, although the grid has rows. Where should the component read the dataset values?
options: In the component's constructor.
In updateView, which runs when the dataset is available and whenever it changes.
In destroy.
In getOutputs.
questions.explanation: Dataset values can't be initialized in init. updateView(context) is called whenever a bound property, dataset, size or state changes, so dataset records are read and rendered there (and the component must tolerate null values while data loads). getOutputs returns changed output values, and destroy only cleans up.

questions.stem: A data-science team needs an agent on a fine-tuned open-source model, orchestrated with LangGraph code they already maintain, hosted with private networking in Azure and callable from other applications through an API. A separate business team wants a Teams-based HR agent that business users can maintain and that follows existing Power Platform data policies. Which pairing is most appropriate?
options: Microsoft Foundry (a hosted agent) for the data-science team; Microsoft Copilot Studio for the HR agent.
Microsoft Copilot Studio for both teams.
Microsoft Copilot Studio for the data-science team; Microsoft Foundry for the HR agent.
A Microsoft Foundry prompt agent for both teams.
questions.explanation: Foundry suits pro-code needs: custom/fine-tuned models, your own framework (LangGraph runs as a hosted agent), Azure-native networking and an API surface. Copilot Studio suits business-user-authored, channel-native (Teams) agents governed by Power Platform data policies, environments and ALM. They integrate, so a solution can use both.

questions.stem: A CI pipeline runs pa app push --solution-id "Contoso Orders" under a service principal and fails. Which TWO changes are required for the pipeline to publish the app into the solution?
options: Pass the solution's GUID (or set PA_CLI_SOLUTION_ID) instead of its display name.
Convert the solution to a managed solution before pushing.
Remove the code app from the solution and import it separately.
Have the app maker share edit access with the service principal by using the Enterprise Application object ID, not the app-registration object ID.
Switch the pipeline to pac code push.
questions.explanation: --solution-id must be a GUID (solution names are rejected; in CI use PA_CLI_SOLUTION_ID). For service-principal publishing the maker must first share edit access with the principal, using the Enterprise Application (service principal) object ID. pac code push is legacy, and solution type isn't the cause.

questions.stem: A plug-in needs an API key that must not be included when the solution is exported and should be readable only by administrators. Where do you provide the key in the Plug-in Registration Tool?
options: As a column in a plug-in image.
In the step's Execution Order field.
In the step's Secure Configuration.
In the step's Unsecure Configuration.
questions.explanation: Secure configuration is stored separately, isn't exported with the solution, is readable only by administrators and reaches the plug-in through the constructor MyPlugin(string unsecure, string secure). Unsecure configuration is exported with the solution.

questions.stem: A flow action calls a rate-limited partner API. Transient failures usually clear within a minute, and the default retry policy (four exponential retries) isn't enough. What should you configure?
options: Set the action's retry policy to Fixed interval with a count of 10 and an interval of PT30S.
Turn on Pagination with a threshold.
Keep the Default policy and extend the flow's run duration.
Replace the action with a Filter array action.
questions.explanation: Retry policy types are default (exponential, 4 retries), none, fixed and exponential; fixed/exponential allow a count of 1–90 with an ISO-8601 interval. Run duration, Filter array and pagination are unrelated to retries.

questions.stem: A synchronization service stores the DataToken returned by RetrieveEntityChangesRequest. After a 10-day outage the next request that uses the stored token fails. With default settings, what should the service do?
options: Perform a full initial retrieval (no token) to rebuild the baseline, then resume incremental sync with the new token.
Increase the page size.
Disable and re-enable change tracking on the table.
Retry with the same token after an hour.
questions.explanation: Change-tracking tokens expire after 7 days by default (Organization.ExpireChangeTrackingInDays). An expired token means you must run a full retrieval (a request without a token) and continue from the new DataToken. Change tracking can't be disabled once enabled.

questions.stem: A developer wants a code app to start an existing cloud flow. Which flow can be added with pa app add flow?
options: A solution-aware instant flow that uses the Power Apps trigger.
An instant flow that isn't in a solution but is owned by the maker.
A scheduled flow in the default solution.
An automated flow that triggers when a Dataverse row is created.
questions.explanation: Code apps support only solution-aware instant flows that use the Power Apps trigger. Scheduled flows, automated flows and instant flows with other triggers aren't supported, and the flow must belong to a solution. End users also need Dataverse permission to run it (for example the App Opener role or an equivalent).

questions.stem: A data-engineering team wants to upsert thousands of rows into Dataverse from a pandas workflow running in Azure and authenticate with a managed identity. Which option is most appropriate?
options: A canvas app that uses Power Fx Patch in a loop.
The Dataverse SDK for Python (PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client, DataverseClient) with an azure.identity credential such as ManagedIdentityCredential.
A plug-in registered on UpsertMultiple.
Microsoft.CrmSdk.CoreAssemblies and CrmServiceClient called from Python.
questions.explanation: The Dataverse SDK for Python works with any azure.identity credential that supplies get_token() (including managed identity), supports bulk CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple/UpsertMultiple, DataFrame wrappers, batching and automatic retries. The .NET assemblies aren't a Python option, and canvas apps or plug-ins aren't data-engineering pipelines.

questions.stem: Select the best user-experience option for each requirement.
questions.template:
1. A reusable, data-bound control that must render inline on model-driven forms alongside native controls: {1}
2. A custom React application with its own routing that runs inside Power Apps with Microsoft Entra sign-in and connector access: {2}
3. An AI-authored React page added to an existing model-driven app: {3}

options: Canvas component library
HTML web resource in an IFRAME
Code app
PCF code component
Code app
PCF code component
Power Pages site
Generative page
Web resource
Code app
MCP app widget
Generative page

questions.explanation: PCF components render in the same context and load with other form components (a web resource in an IFRAME doesn't). A code app is a whole custom web app in your own framework hosted by Power Apps with Entra authentication and connectors. A generative page is an AI-authored React page inside a model-driven app. MCP app widgets render tool results in agent surfaces such as Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

questions.stem: You evaluate Dataverse support in a code app that uses the generated AccountsService. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: getMetadata can return column display names and relationship metadata for the table.
getAll accepts a FetchXML query.
The app can create new custom columns on the table through the generated service.
getAll supports an OData filter string and a select list to limit columns.

questions.explanation: Code apps can read table metadata (getMetadata) and query with IGetAllOptions (select, filter, orderBy, top, maxPageSize, skip, skipToken). Not supported yet: FetchXML, alternate keys, polymorphic lookups and schema (metadata) create/update/delete.

questions.stem: A custom .NET application must hold a conversation with a published, standard-harness Copilot Studio agent in production. Which approach is supported and generally available?
options: Publish the agent through the Preview A2A client channel and call it from the app.
Call the Dataverse MCP server and ask it to run the agent.
Embed the web chat in an iframe and read the page's DOM.
Use Microsoft.Agents.CopilotStudio.Client (CopilotClient with ConnectionSettings) and an Entra app registration that has the CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke permission.
questions.explanation: The Copilot Studio client library (direct-to-engine channel) is the documented production path. ConnectionSettings holds the environment ID and schema name (or a DirectConnectUrl); the Entra app registration needs the delegated CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke permission. The MCP/A2A client channels are Preview and limited to the GitHub Copilot harness.

questions.stem: For each statement about custom code in a custom connector, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: The script must finish within 2 minutes and the script file can't exceed 1 MB.
A connector can contain several script files, one per operation.
The class must be named Script and derive from ScriptBase.
Custom code works with connectors that use the on-premises data gateway.

questions.explanation: Custom code is limited to one script file (≤ 1 MB) that must complete in 2 minutes (a raised limit that new connectors get automatically). The class is Script : ScriptBase overriding ExecuteAsync; outbound calls should use this.Context.SendAsync. Custom code isn't supported with the on-premises data gateway.

questions.stem: Complete the plug-in that implements a custom API. The API has a request parameter OrderTotal (Money) and a response property Discount (Money).

options: InputParameters
PreEntityImages
SharedVariables
OutputParameters
InputParameters
SharedVariables
OutputParameters
PostEntityImages

questions.explanation: A custom API's plug-in reads the request parameters from InputParameters (keyed by each parameter's UniqueName) and sets the response properties through OutputParameters. The plug-in type is linked to the API through PluginTypeId and runs at stage 30; you don't register a step for it.

questions.stem: You are building a new custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that Copilot Studio agents will call. Which design is correct?
options: Expose the server with the Server-Sent Events (SSE) transport and register it through a custom connector.
Expose the server over Streamable HTTP and register it with the MCP onboarding wizard, or in a custom connector whose OpenAPI declares x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0.
Implement it as a Dataverse custom API and register it with the Plug-in Registration Tool.
Expose the server over WebSockets and import it as an OpenAPI 3.0 definition.
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio supports the Streamable HTTP transport for MCP; SSE was deprecated for MCP after August 2025. You register a server through the Add tool → Model Context Protocol wizard or through a custom connector whose OpenAPI carries x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0. Custom connector import also requires OpenAPI 2.0, and a Dataverse custom API isn't an MCP server.

questions.stem: Users report that a published code app sometimes never finishes loading. Application Insights, which the team instrumented in the app, shows no errors for those sessions. Where should you look first?
options: The Azure Functions logs.
Power Platform Monitor for the code app (admin center → Monitor → Power Apps), including the app open success rate.
The plug-in trace log.
The solution layers view.
questions.explanation: Application Insights telemetry for code apps is manual and only captures events after a successful app load, so startup failures don't appear there. Power Platform Monitor is zero-code and reports code-app metrics such as time to interactive, session count, open success rate and data-request success/latency.

questions.stem: A plug-in creates a service by calling factory.CreateOrganizationService(null) and then updates a record. Under which user context do the service calls run?
options: The user in context.UserId.
The SYSTEM user.
The user in context.InitiatingUserId.
The user who registered the plug-in step.
questions.explanation: When called in a plug-in, a null user ID means the SYSTEM user; Guid.Empty means the same user as context.UserId; any other value is that specific user. UserId is the user the step runs as (impersonated user or caller) and InitiatingUserId is who actually triggered the operation.

questions.stem: You troubleshoot a code app with browser developer tools and filter the Network tab. Select the filter for each kind of traffic.
questions.template:
Connector (API hub) calls — filter by: {1}
Dataverse calls — filter by: {2}

options: powerapps.com
azurewebsites.net
dynamics.com
apihub.net
dynamics.com
windows.net
apihub.net

questions.explanation: In the Network tab, apihub.net shows connector traffic and dynamics.com shows Dataverse traffic. Use the Console's Errors filter to find Content Security Policy violations.

questions.stem: In a cloud flow, actions inside a scope named Try may fail. A scope named Catch must run only when Try fails, is skipped or times out. Which setting do you configure?
options: Enable concurrency control on Catch.
Set Try's retry policy to None.
Configure run after on Catch: select has failed, is skipped and has timed out for Try.
Add a Terminate action before Try.
questions.explanation: The try/catch/finally pattern uses Scope actions and Configure run after: Catch runs after Try has failed / is skipped / has timed out, and Finally runs after all four statuses of Try and Catch. Use result('Try') in Catch to inspect failures.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Client API, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: control.setNotification shows a message on a column and blocks the record from being saved until it is cleared.
formContext.ui.setFormNotification prevents the user from saving the form.
Xrm.Navigation.openForm can open a main form as a modal dialog.

questions.explanation: Only control-level notifications (setNotification) block saving; form notifications and app notifications don't. A main form can be shown as a dialog only with Xrm.Navigation.navigateTo (target: 2); openForm can't do it and its success callback fires only for quick-create saves.

questions.stem: For each statement about Dataverse API limits and retries, select Yes if it is true.

statements.text: ServiceClient automatically waits for the Retry-After period and resends a throttled request.
A client that calls the Web API directly must implement its own retry that honors the Retry-After header.
Sending operations in large batches avoids consuming Dataverse request capacity (entitlement) limits.
Plug-ins that call the Organization service are subject to the 6,000-requests-per-5-minutes service protection limit like external clients.

questions.explanation: A throttled call returns 429 + Retry-After; ServiceClient/CrmServiceClient handle it automatically, raw Web API clients must do it themselves. Batching doesn't bypass entitlement limits — each operation still counts. Plug-ins are exempt from service protection limits (though their execution time counts toward the triggering request).

questions.stem: You import version 2.0 of a managed solution into production. A form still behaves like version 1.0. The form's Solution layers view shows an Active (unmanaged) layer above the managed layer. What should you do?
options: Import the managed solution again with Overwrite customizations selected.
Uninstall and reinstall the managed solution.
Use Remove active customizations on the form to delete the unmanaged layer.
Create a patch of version 2.0 and import it.
questions.explanation: Layers are evaluated top-down and for most components the top layer wins. An unmanaged (Active) layer sits above all managed layers, so it overrides the managed update. Remove active customizations removes that top unmanaged layer (it is irreversible). Re-importing won't touch the unmanaged layer.

questions.stem: Arrange the steps to package a code component for release through a solution (not the quick pac pcf push development path).
items: Scaffold the project with pac pcf init.
Implement the component and test it in the harness with npm start watch.
Create a solution project with pac solution init.
Add the component project to the solution project with pac solution add-reference.
Build the solution project in Release configuration (msbuild /restore).
Import the generated solution into the target environment.
questions.explanation: The release path uses a .cdsproj solution project that references one or more .pcfproj component projects; building it in Release produces the solution zip you import (manually or via Build Tools). pac pcf push is the fast development path that deploys to a temporary PowerAppsTools_<prefix> solution.

questions.stem: A parent flow calls a child flow with Run a Child Flow. The run fails with an error saying only embedded connections are supported. What should you do?
options: Move the child flow out of the solution.
Convert the child flow to a scheduled flow.
Pass the parent's connections to the child at run time.
On the child flow's Run only users settings, set each connection to Use this connection (the child's own connection).
questions.explanation: Parent and child must be in a solution, and every connection on the child's Run only users tile must be switched to Use this connection; passing a parent's connections to a child isn't supported. The child uses the Manually trigger a flow trigger and returns data with Respond to a PowerApp or flow.

questions.stem: You expose a REST API implemented as an Azure Function through Azure API Management. API Management currently provides an OpenAPI 3.0 definition. What must you do to create a custom connector from it?
options: Import it as a Postman collection.
Import the OpenAPI 3.0 file directly in the custom connector wizard.
Export or convert the definition to OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) — for example, download the OpenAPI v2 file from API Management — and import that.
Register it as a Dataverse custom API.
questions.explanation: The custom connector wizard imports OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) only; OpenAPI 3.0 isn't supported, so convert/export a 2.0 definition first (files must also be under 1 MB). The documented path for an Azure Function is to front it with API Management and import the downloaded definition.

questions.stem: Requirement 1. You must set a default priority and block creation (with a clear message) when the asset is not under contract. How should you implement this?
options: An asynchronous plug-in on Create registered at PostOperation that sets the priority and deletes invalid work orders.
A cloud flow that triggers when a work order is created and updates the priority.
A JavaScript OnSave handler on the dispatcher form.
A synchronous plug-in on Create registered at PreOperation that sets the priority on Target and throws InvalidPluginExecutionException when the contract check fails.
questions.explanation: The rule must hold for every way a work order is created, so it needs server-side, synchronous logic. A PreOperation step can edit the Target (the default is saved with the row) and throw to stop the operation with a user-visible message. Asynchronous plug-ins and flows act after the row is saved, and client script only covers the app UI.

questions.stem: Requirement 2. Which option should you recommend to notify the ERP when a work order is closed?
options: Register an Azure Service Bus queue service endpoint and an asynchronous PostOperation step that publishes when the work order is closed.
Register a webhook that posts to the ERP's REST API.
Register a two-way service endpoint.
Register an Event Hub endpoint.
questions.explanation: A Service Bus queue persists messages while the consumer is offline and lets the ERP team pull them later, so nothing is lost. A webhook (and a two-way/REST contract) needs the listener online at the time of the event; Event Hub is a streaming ingestion endpoint. Service Bus posting from Dataverse is asynchronous and authenticates with SAS.

questions.stem: Requirement 3. Which table type should you use for the nightly meter readings?
options: An elastic table with a time-to-live (TTL) of 90 days.
A standard table plus a scheduled flow that deletes old rows.
A standard table with an alternate key on the device ID.
A virtual table over the IoT platform.
questions.explanation: Elastic tables (Azure Cosmos DB behind Dataverse) are designed for very high volume, bursty, non-relational data and support TTL (ttlinseconds) for automatic expiry. They trade away relationships and multi-record transactions, which this scenario doesn't need. A virtual table leaves data in the IoT system; a standard table plus a deletion flow wouldn't scale or expire data natively.

questions.stem: Requirement 4. Which approach should you recommend for the technician UI?
options: A Power Apps code app, published by the CI pipeline with the Power Apps CLI (pa app push) under a service principal.
An HTML web resource that embeds a React bundle.
A generative page in the dispatcher's model-driven app.
A PCF field component on the work order form.
questions.explanation: A code app is a whole custom web app in your own framework (React), hosted by Power Apps with Entra authentication, Dataverse/connector access and platform governance. Your pipeline can build it and publish with pa app push (Power Platform's own Git integration isn't supported for code apps, but the team keeps source in its own Git repo, so it isn't needed). A PCF is a control, a generative page is an AI-authored page inside a model-driven app, and a web resource lacks connections and platform integration.

questions.stem: Requirement 5. Which TWO actions should you take so the Python Foundry agent can read work orders (read-only) and consult the Copilot Studio agent?
options: Add the Dataverse MCP server as an MCP tool of the Foundry agent and restrict the allowed tools to read-only operations (for example search_data and read_query).
Call the published Copilot Studio agent from the agent's code by using the Copilot Studio client library with an Entra app registration that has CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke.
Publish the Copilot Studio agent through the Preview MCP client channel and add the Work IQ tool to query Dataverse tables.
Create an application user with the System Administrator role and store its client secret in the agent's instructions.
Use ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2 from a Power Apps code app that the agent calls.
questions.explanation: The Dataverse MCP server (https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp) is the supported way to give an agent governed Dataverse access; limiting the tool list (for example to search_data and read_query, which is SELECT-only) keeps it read-only. The Copilot Studio client library is the GA, production way for custom code to converse with a published agent. Secrets in instructions, Preview channels, Work IQ (Microsoft 365 data, not Dataverse tables) and a code-app connector method don't meet the requirements or the GA preference.
